verdict.rationale: ROS 2 docs advertise a full toolkit (launch system, CLI tools, client libraries in multiple languages, drivers/community packages, simulators, bagging) that in principle should speed up bring-up of a new robot, and community voices confirm you get things 'for free' like bags, viewers, teleop, sim [ros2-docs-6, ros2-docs-8, ros2-docs-16, ros2-comm-9, ros2-comm-10]. However, hands-on community reports concretely contradict the 'hours not weeks' framing: users describe dependency hell, convoluted builds, and struggling for a long time with unorganized tutorials and unexpected errors when trying to get ROS running, and one report states 'actually deploying a ROS based system is about as difficult as rewriting the whole thing from scratch' [ros2-comm-6, ros2-comm-7, ros2-comm-12, ros2-comm-15]. Missing for 10: first-party bring-up-time benchmarks, no vendor-provided quick-start bring-up case study, and independent success stories showing hours-scale hardware bring-up to counter the contradicting reports.
